body.heading: Start with three colours
paragraphs: You only need red, blue, and yellow paint to begin. Put a small blob of each on your plate or palette.
Paint three circles, one in each colour. These are called the primary colours. Every other colour can be made by mixing them.

body.heading: Mix and see
paragraphs: Mix red and yellow together. What colour do you get? Now try blue and yellow, then red and blue.
Paint a circle for each new colour you make. You have just made orange, green, and purple. They are called the secondary colours.

body.heading: Invent your own colour
paragraphs: Mix a tiny bit of one colour into another and see what happens. Add white to make it lighter, or a little black to make it darker.
Give your new colour a name, like “dinosaur green” or “midnight sky.” Artists invent new colours all the time, and now you have too.

description: For ages 6–9 with an adult: mix red, blue, and yellow paint to discover brand-new colours.

safetyNotes: Use washable, child-safe paint, wear old clothes or an apron, and wash hands when you finish.
